---
title: "The Theory of DHE"
format: html
editor: visual
---

The **Digital Health Enablement (DHE)** model proposes that an individual's capacity to benefit from digital health interventions is shaped by seven inter-related domains. These domains capture the **cognitive**, **social**, and **behavioural** factors that determine whether a person can meaningfully engage with digital health tools.

The model situates these domains within a broader context of structural drivers --- **economic**, **social**, **cultural**, and **personal** factors --- that shape enablement upstream. Together, greater enablement across these domains is theorised to predict improved uptake, engagement, and effectiveness of digital health interventions.

![**Figure 1** The Digital Health Enablement model (Mercer, et al., 2026)](images/dhe_model.png){width="100%" fig-alt="A hub and spoke diagram showing the seven domains of the DHE model surrounding a central Digital Health Enablement node, with structural drivers on the left and outcomes on the right."}


| Sub-Construct | Definition |
|:-|:---|
| Digital Skills | Perception of one's abilities to effectively engage and use digital technologies safely in areas including health information gathering, communication, content creation, and problem solving |
| Digital Health Literacy | The extent to which one understands digital technologies and approaches digital health resources critically, including in the selection, evaluation, and application of digital technologies |
| Digital Self-Efficacy | The extent to which individuals are confident in their ability to use digital technologies effectively |
| Sociodigital Norms | The behaviours around digital technologies that are either typical or seen as proper in each context |
| Digital Outcome Expectancy | An individual's beliefs about the likely physical, social, or self-evaluative outcomes of engaging with digital health technologies |
| Digital Trust | The confidence that users have in the integrity, security, and privacy of digital technologies |
| Digital Behavioural Regulation | The extent to which individual behaviours around digital health technologies are regulated by internal or external factors |
